paragraphs.source_en: The escape pod opens, magnetic lock thudding back. The door hisses upward. I pick Theodora from the couch and strap her into one of the seats. The straps are too big, made for Golds. Then something deep and horrible roars in the belly of my ship, half a kilometer away. Our torpedo stores detonate.

units.source_en: The escape pod opens, magnetic lock thudding back.
The door hisses upward.
I pick Theodora from the couch and strap her into one of the seats.

ja.t: はソファからセオドラを

units.source_en: The straps are too big, made for Golds.
Then something deep and horrible roars in the belly of my ship, half a kilometer away.
Our torpedo stores detonate.

paragraphs.source_en: Gone is the artificial gravity. Gone are the stable walls. It’s an insidious sensation. Everything spins. I slam into the escape pod’s floor, ceiling? I don’t know. Pressure vents out of the ship. Someone vomits. I smell it rather than hear it. I shout at the Grays to get in the pod. Only one stays behind now, face drawn and quiet, as the sergeant and a corporal pull themselves into the escape pod. They strap in across from me. I activate the launch function and salute the Gray who stays behind. He salutes back, proud and loyal despite the quiet in him as he faces his last moment of life, eyes distant and thinking of some young love, some path not taken, perhaps wondering why he was not born Gold.

I don’t know.

I smell it rather than hear it.
I shout at the Grays to get in the pod.
Only one stays behind now, face drawn and quiet, as the sergeant and a corporal pull themselves into the escape pod.
They strap in across from me.
I activate the launch function and salute the Gray who stays behind.

He salutes back, proud and loyal despite the quiet in him as he faces his last moment of life, eyes distant and thinking of some young love, some path not taken, perhaps wondering why he was not born Gold.

ja.t: えているのかもしれない。

paragraphs.source_en: Then the door closes and he is gone from my world.

units.source_en: Then the door closes and he is gone from my world.

paragraphs.source_en: I’m slammed into my seat as the escape pod shoots away from the dying ship. Ripping through debris. Then we’re weightless again and drifting away from trouble as inertial dampeners kick in. Out our viewport I see my flagship burping plumes of blue and red flame. Processed helium-3, which powers both ships, ignites near my man-of-war’s engines, causing a chain-effect explosion that rips the ship apart. Suddenly I realize it wasn’t debris I felt against my escape pod as I left the ship. It was people. My crew. Hundreds of lowColors spilled into space.

ja.t: ポッドにぶつかっていたものが

units.source_en: It was people.
My crew.
Hundreds of lowColors spilled into space.
The Grays sit opposite me.

paragraphs.source_en: “He had three girls,” the dark-skinned corporal says, shuddering as the adrenaline fades away. “Two years and he was out with a pension. And you popped him in the head.”

units.source_en: “He had three girls,” the dark-skinned corporal says, shuddering as the adrenaline fades away.
“Two years and he was out with a pension.
And you popped him in the head.”

paragraphs.source_en: “After my report, coward won’t even scrape a death pension,” the sergeant sneers.

units.source_en: “After my report, coward won’t even scrape a death pension,” the sergeant sneers.

paragraphs.source_en: The corporal blinks at her. “You cold bitch.”

units.source_en: The corporal blinks at her.
“You cold bitch.”

paragraphs.source_en: Their words fade, overcome by the beating of blood in my ears. This is my fault. I broke the rules at the Institute. I changed the paradigm and thought they wouldn’t adapt. That they wouldn’t change their strategy for me.

paragraphs.source_en: And now I have lost so many lives, I may never know the tally.

units.source_en: And now I have lost so many lives, I may never know the tally.

paragraphs.source_en: More people have died in a blink than during a whole year of the Institute, their deaths opening a black hole in my stomach.

units.source_en: More people have died in a blink than during a whole year of the Institute, their deaths opening a black hole in my stomach.

paragraphs.source_en: Roque and Victra hail me over the coms. They will have tracked my datapad and know I am safe. I barely hear them. Anger, thick and evil, swirls inside me, making my hands shake, my heart slam.
